assumptions: Criteria remain pending until the lead runs the canonical gate. Neither the full gate, a heavy suite nor the policy check was run. The teeth driver was run for finding 314 only. Suite 86_veldo_0127 and all live captures are untouched.

The event command, its consumer and authority service socket wiring belong to VELDO-0323. The suite serves the real spool socket with a signature-checking, idempotent event receiver stand-in. The no-command row uses the real Ledger without that stand-in. No production event consumption or removal is claimed.

Installing hooks in client accounts is VELDO-0329. The pack registers both hooks with exec and a 15 second client limit. The script has a 12 second deadline. Tests start real Python hook processes whose parent is the fixture client; no live client installation or client parent topology was measured.

The installer supplies VELDO_SPACE_STATE_ROOT and veldo on PATH or VELDO_SPACE_CLI. With no state root the hook uses the user's XDG state folder, veldo. A notification that is no entry is kept under refused/ with why; one no spool takes, or one whose module cannot be loaded, is kept as a line of space-session.unspooled.jsonl under the state root, else under the fallback. Only when neither root can be written at all is nothing kept. Nothing reads the unspooled file or refused/ back yet: both are records for a person, and no removal can follow from either.

New sessions use the first scratch root. working_folder in the configured session pattern is UTF-8 hex to avoid aliases. Existing unrecorded folders are refused, even at delayed replay. The hook declares but creates no scratch folder. A preexisting item with another process identity is refused rather than reassigned.

The latch row runs session_hook directly in a fixture child; the pack script envelope is exercised by the start rows and offline start/end rows. The AC3 mutant attempts recursive deletion of the planted client folder, held by the file latch in the forked child, and fails the 15 second return bound. No fixture work is actually deleted by the mutant.

The store journal signer is a fixture function; observer commands use a real OpenSSH key and the Ledger verifies them. Invalid signatures and expired packets are refused. No act checks are overridden and no real Docker engine is contacted.
Released entries preserve the creator name for VELDO-0335, defaulting to record for the existing record verb. This ticket does not authorize or consume a release.

The CLI retains its existing direct in-process event path when explicitly wired. On an absent event command or an exception it spools; remote replay uses fresh observer signatures and the existing deadline and retry handling.
This bundle follows a review of the build (verdict FIX, six findings) and its fix round. The fix-validation record (runner results and the assessor's verdict) is the lead's and is not in this bundle.

Review finding 5 proposed refusing --path on session types. It is said on standard error and not refused: suite 151 (VELDO-0313), outside this footprint, holds rows in which a session event with a path is accepted and one on the protect list is refused by name. The lead decides whether to refuse it in a ticket that owns that suite.
Known and left: when `veldo space event` itself cannot spool, it says so on standard error and exits 0, as in the build. The hook does not go through that verb.

fix4/deadline-in-read replaces the module's read for one call to raise TimeoutError: the 12 second timer cannot be made to fire inside the read on demand. The hook script's own timer was not measured firing there.
rollback: Revert the implementation commit. Session hooks then leave no notification; the existing spool records remain.
